subject: APAC micro-region capacity ask: Taiwan + Seoul pilot, HK on-prem fallback
messages:
From: Chia-Wei <chia-wei@lumina.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Simon Lee <simon.lee@seoullabs.co>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 23:12:00 +0800
Subject: APAC micro-region capacity ask: Taiwan + Seoul pilot, HK on-prem fallback

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this call last week. As discussed, Lumina wants to run a small multiregion pilot starting late March to validate latency and cost for our conversational agent in Taiwan and Seoul, with an on-prem option in Hong Kong for compliance-sensitive customers. High-level ask:

- Start date target: 2027-03-28 (4 week pilot)
- Workload: 50k monthly active users, expected peak 180 concurrent requests (avg seq length 1k tokens, sometimes up to 4k)
- Model: we prefer an H100-backed flavor for quality, but cost sensitivity suggests a mixed A100/H100 pool is acceptable
- Desired SLO: p95 < 250ms token generation for short prompts, 99.5% availability during pilot

Attached an updated requirement doc (lumina_capacity_request_v2.pdf) with traffic curves and compliance note. Primary questions for you: whether Redwood can provide a dedicated pool split across Taiwan + Seoul (cross-region routing for failover), recommended node mixes, and whether HK on-prem is feasible as an NDA'd fallback. Also need an early estimate of committed monthly cost and lead times.

Simon (cc) will coordinate regional infra details on our side. Please let us know next steps and a timeline to get an SOW in place.

Best,
Chia-Wei
Head of Platform
Lumina AI

Attachments: lumina_capacity_request_v2.pdf
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Chia-Wei <chia-wei@lumina.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 00:28:00 +0800
Subject: Re: APAC micro-region capacity ask: Taiwan + Seoul pilot, HK on-prem fallback

Hi Chia-Wei — thanks for the clear brief and the attachment. We're excited to run this with you. A few clarifying items before we build concrete sizing options:

1) Traffic shape: can you share a 48-hour peak sample (UTC timestamps) and the % of calls that are streaming vs full-response generation?
2) Seq length distribution: you quoted avg 1k / peak 4k — can you confirm percentiles at p50/p90/p99 if available?
3) Auth/compliance: which data residency rules trigger the need for HK on-prem (customer lists or regulatory requirement)?
4) SLA and rollback: do you need a hard SLA in pilot or a baseline for measurement?

Internal owners: Karthik and Hannah — can you sketch an initial node-mix hypothesis and lead times? I'll draft a mutual action plan and ask ops for an on-prem feasibility check for HK.

Proposed next step: 30-min sync tomorrow (Thu) 10:00 SGT to align on those questions. Does that work?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions (APAC)
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: APAC micro-region capacity ask: Taiwan + Seoul pilot, HK on-prem fallback

Quick sizing notes after scanning the request doc and the initial numbers from Chia-Wei:

Assumptions
- p95 token latency target implies we need aggressive batching + KV cache reuse; longer seqs increase memory pressure and hurt concurrency.
- Taiwan infra: H100 availability in TW zones limited; Seoul has more H100 quota.

Options (provisional, all nodes are GPU hosts with 40 A100 / H100 token-equivalents per node for rough math):

Option A — Cost-conservative mixed pool (recommended entry)- Seoul (cloud): 6 A100 nodes + 2 H100 burst nodes (reserve 120 concurrent capacity, ~p95 headroom)- Taiwan (cloud): 4 A100 nodes + 1 H100 burst node- Buffer / failover lane: cross-region routing with prefix caching; expected steady-state cost lower by ~28% vs H100-only

Option B — Performance-first (higher cost)- Seoul: 4 H100 nodes + 4 A100 nodes- Taiwan: 2 H100 nodes + 2 A100 nodes- This gives higher headroom for long seqs but adds lead time for H100 allocation

Option C — Rapid pilot / minimal commit- Seoul: 4 A100 nodes (use quantized model variant for pilot)- Taiwan: 2 A100 nodes- HK on-prem kept as cold backup behind an NDA (no initial procurement)

Lead times and procurement notes- A100 cloud nodes: 2-3 weeks to reserve in region; H100 nodes: 4-8 weeks depending on quota and procurement windows.- On-prem HK: requires SOW + site validation; earliest pilot ~8-10 weeks if customer provides rack access and network ACLs quickly.

Action items- I'll produce a short cost/throughput workbook (cost_model_apac_nodes.xlsx) with per-option monthly run rates and token-unit economics.- Marcus, can you confirm whether Taiwan cloud region supports our burst H100 capacity or if we need partner colocation?

Karthik
Lead, Dedicated Products
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cost_model_apac_nodes.xlsx
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 01:12:00 +0800
Subject: Re: APAC micro-region capacity ask: Taiwan + Seoul pilot, HK on-prem fallback

Thanks Karthik — a couple of operational constraints to flag before we share options with Lumina:

- Lead time sensitivity: if Lumina needs start on 2027-03-28 we should push Option C for the pilot; Options A/B require committed reserves that likely slip the start date.
- SLA & monitoring: we should propose a measurement window (2 weeks) in which we collect p95/p99 metrics before offering a firm SLA.
- Node reuse: recommend setting clear contract language that allows node reallocation outside the pilot (30-day notice) to mitigate capacity risk for us.
- Pricing flexibility: propose a pilot discount and a conversion credit if they commit to a 6-month reserved tranche within 30 days of pilot end.

Marcus — could you do a quick ops check on Taiwan H100 availability and HK on-prem vendor list? If HK is slow, we should keep it as an NDA'd option and plan cloud fallback with strict data controls.

Hannah
APAC Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Chia-Wei <chia-wei@lumina.ai>, Simon Lee <simon.lee@seoullabs.co>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 08:32:00 +0800
Subject: Re: APAC micro-region capacity ask: Taiwan + Seoul pilot, HK on-prem fallback

Chia-Wei / Simon — thank you, here's a concise mutual action plan and our proposed pilot configuration so you can share internally: 

Mutual action plan (pilot)- Kickoff and data exchange: by 2027-03-02 (Lumina provides 48-hr sample + percentile data and confirms compliance triggers)- Pilot start: targeted 2027-03-28 (4 weeks) using Option C (rapid pilot) unless Lumina prefers an upfront reserve- Pilot config (provisioning): Seoul: 4 A100 nodes (cloud) / Taiwan: 2 A100 nodes (cloud) with cross-region prefix caching and reroute policy.- Burstable H100 capacity: reserved as on-call nodes in Seoul (2 nodes) if needed for peak testing; formal H100 commit can be discussed post-pilot.- HK on-prem: we will treat as fallback; provide SOW template and initial vendor checklist by 2027-03-05.

Provisional economics- Pilot rate (provisional, excl. discounts): see attached cost_model_apac_nodes.xlsx — we'll follow up with a pilot discount and conversion credit language for the SOW.

Next steps- Lumina to send the 48hr traffic sample and confirm whether the pilot must include hard SLA language.
- We will prepare an SOW + DocuSign link targeting signature by 2027-03-10 to allow procurement time.

If that aligns, we'll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff on 2027-03-03 with Infra/Network and Solutions.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions (APAC)
Redwood Inference
